handoff_instructions.purpose: Handoffs document the current state and scope of the project so a new LLM session can pick up exactly where the last one left off. They are the primary continuity mechanism for this project.
what_to_include: A summary of what was done, discussed, decided, or built in this session
What worked and what did not work
Current pipeline state — what scripts exist, what their status is, what the next steps are
A condensed recap of prior sessions so the new LLM has full project context without reading every previous handoff
Open questions or blockers that carry into the next session
what_not_to_include: Exhaustive code listings — reference file paths instead
Decisions that were reversed or abandoned mid-session — only document final state
Speculation about distant future work — stay close to what is actually next
format_rules: This handoff_instructions block must appear at the top of every future handoff
When a user says 'create a handoff for this session,' use this block as the template and fill in the session-specific fields
Prior session summaries should be condensed — one paragraph per session, not a full retelling
Be brief but complete. A new LLM should be able to start working immediately after reading this file

title: Phase 1 Kickoff — Quick Job Budget Generation: Initial Product Requirement Identification
status: PLANNING — PRD drafted, no code written. Requirements identified through conversation. Pending Nolan review of the PRD and the open questions.
phase: Phase 1 — Quick Job Budget Generation (rough whole-job budget from a single plan sheet). Distinct product from Phase 0 (plan -> quantity sheet).

foundational_concept_what_learning_means.read_first: This project says the system 'learns typical practices.' Define it precisely so a new session does not misread it.
foundational_concept_what_learning_means.core_truth: There is NO model training or fine-tuning anywhere in this project, now or planned. Claude/Gemini weights are frozen; nothing the system processes ever updates them. Every behavior that looks like 'learning' is ONE mechanism: persist knowledge as data, then retrieve it back into the model's context window at inference time. This is in-context learning / RAG, not weight updates.
two_halves_map_to_data_operations: Learning from the past = System A writes accumulated knowledge to durable data (the CASE LIBRARY of resolved past jobs + the KNOWLEDGE PACK of derivation rules, $/unit distributions, typical-section defaults). System B retrieves the relevant pieces into the prompt when estimating a new sheet. The model appears to 'know' Terra Underground's practices only because we hand it that knowledge every time.

Learning going forward (feedback loop) = when Brian corrects an estimate, we WRITE THAT CORRECTION BACK into the case library / knowledge pack. Future estimates retrieve the updated data and reflect the correction. This is a file/DB write -- instant, inspectable, reversible -- NOT retraining.
build_implications: Do NOT pursue fine-tuning. Engineering effort goes into three things only: (a) how knowledge is REPRESENTED (case-library schema), (b) how the right pieces get RETRIEVED into context, (c) the WRITE-BACK loop.
The 'learning' is debuggable: knowledge is plain data, so you can open a file and see or fix exactly what the system 'believes'. A wrong estimate traces to a wrong record/pattern you edit directly.

This is the SAME mechanism Claude Code itself uses for continuity (a persistent memory directory reloaded each session + handoff docs). The product is an engineered, domain-specific version: case library ~= memory files, retrieval ~= loading the relevant ones, write-back ~= saving a note after a correction.
foundational_concept_what_learning_means.one_line: The model never changes -- the knowledge base does, and the model reasons over whatever slice of it we place in context.
foundational_concept_what_learning_means.prd_location: Captured as PRD section 1.1 'What "learning" means in this project (foundational)'.

what_nolan_asked_for.goal: Begin Phase 1: generate ROUGH BUDGETS (dollar figures) for a job given a new set of plans or even a single plan sheet. Brian frequently gets handed one sheet and asked 'roughly what will this job cost?'. Believes a RAG + LLM setup is likely the right shape but is not committed; wants thorough planning first.
what_nolan_asked_for.learning_intent: Wants the AI to 'learn' typical past practices (in-context, not retraining) to draw conclusions, both from history and going forward.

this_session.summary: Conversation-first requirements identification for Phase 1. Read the Phase 0 master summary handoff and project memory. Confirmed proposal data now exists in-repo and is parseable. Verified every proposal is in the correct job folder. Resolved the data naming confusion. Aligned on the product shape (two-system architecture), accuracy target, output format, and the RAG decision. Wrote the PRD and this handoff. NO code written.
key_findings: PROPOSALS ARE PARSEABLE TEXT: located at data/<folder>/proposals/ as .doc + .pdf (most with revisions). The .doc files are HeavyBid/Word form exports with columns Description | Quan | Unit | Unit Price | Ext Price and embedded raw numeric field values (e.g. =21000 -> $21,000.00). Unit prices AND extended prices are directly extractable. NO vision needed for the cost side. This makes dollar output groundable, not guesswork.
BID PRICES, NOT INTERNAL COST: proposal unit prices blend cost + overhead + profit. That is exactly right for a customer-facing rough budget.

NUMBERING NUANCE: local folder numbers (26001, 25068, ...) are PROPOSAL/BID numbers, not true job numbers. Woodman's true job number is 26008 (local folder is 26001-1; was previously mislabeled 22066). Numbers also change across revisions (Lone Fir proposal 25038 -> 25071). USE JOB NAME AS THE STABLE KEY; the local folder convention is proposal-number-based.

FOLDER VERIFICATION (all correct): 24053-3=Settlement Mountain, 25016-2=Killdeer Meadows, 25037-2=Expo Private Drive, 25068-2=Painted Rock, 25071-1=Lone Fir, 26001-1=Woodman, 26003-1=Mountainside, 26006-2=Solara PH1. Foundry (24066-1) excluded for now per Nolan.

TYPICAL-SECTION GAP IS A FEATURE, NOT A BLOCKER: Nolan corrected an early framing. The fixed DWG pipeline already produced ~88k SF ROW vs 81k ground truth (good). When dimensions are NOT on the sheet, the model should infer from learned patterns ('subdivision roads are almost always 68 ft wide'; section depths follow prior-job patterns). Gap-filling by learned domain regularity is core expected behavior.
decisions: TWO-SYSTEM ARCHITECTURE. System A (offline knowledge building): join DWG extractions (accurate quantities) + proposals (line-item $/unit + totals) + plans/qty sheets/relation docs into a per-job CASE LIBRARY, then derive PATTERNS (derivation rules, $/unit distributions, typical-section defaults, job-type signatures). System B (runtime inference): given one sheet, classify it, Gemini-extract visible facts, retrieve closest analog cases, gap-fill missing quantities/dimensions from learned patterns, apply learned $/unit, output line-item + total + confidence band + plain-language reasoning + provenance. Phase 0's DWG pipeline is machinery for System A, NOT on the runtime path.
NO RUNTIME QTY-SHEET GENERATION. Single-sheet input cannot support a real takeoff; Phase 1 reasons by analogy instead. (Phase 0 qty-sheet generation still used as System-A machinery / for DWG jobs.)
OUTPUT = LINE ITEM + TOTAL, with a confidence band and full traceability (every number tagged 'read from sheet' or 'inferred from job/pattern X').

ACCURACY TARGET = 10-15% error vs the true historical proposal total. Validation by hold-one-sheet-out (feed System B a single sheet from a known job, compare predicted total/items to actual proposal) and leave-one-job-out.

RAG DECISION: do NOT build vector/embedding RAG now. At ~10-30 jobs, load ALL compact case records into context. ~30-50: add attribute filtering. ~50+ fully-resolved jobs is the trigger to stand up ChromaDB/embedding RAG. The case-library data model is identical at every scale, so retrieval is a swappable layer with zero upstream rework. Acquiring more jobs is pure upside regardless of retrieval mechanism.
KEEP ALL PROPOSAL REVISIONS: they encode how/why estimates changed (scope, repricing) — useful signal.
TIME/GEOGRAPHY: date-tag every $/unit and recency-weight (no heavy modeling with few points). Geography handled as a stated assumption / optional manual knob until data supports a learned multiplier.
EXTRACTION PHILOSOPHY: thorough not conservative — pull all possible data from all ~10 DWGs and all proposals; prune later (per Nolan).

phase0_key_facts_for_phase1: DWG extractor is blind: counts everything, LLM interprets semantics from layer/block names. Firm-agnostic (C- NCS prefix and SS-/WA-/SF- discipline prefix both handled).
Block insert counts are exact and authoritative for point features (manholes, FH, bends). Keynote callout counts double-count plan/profile views.

Typical section (ROW width, road width, pavement spec, sidewalk width, swale, stripping depth) lives on the typical-section detail sheet and is the historically hardest thing to extract from geometry — Phase 1 fills these from learned patterns when not visible.
Gemini 2.5 Pro is the vision model of choice; Claude does reasoning/aggregation.
Ground-truth example values exist (e.g. Woodman: 48" manholes 4 EA, 8" sewer 743 LF, 8" water 979 LF, curb/gutter 1875 LF, ROW ~81,757 SF, scuppers 31 EA, services 22 EA).
